newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian PM shaves head, enters monkhood.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian PM shaves head, enters monkhood.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh had his head and eyebrows shaved in a ceremony at the royal palace on Thursday, marking his formal entry into the monkhood for one week.

Ranariddh, who is following a long royal family tradition by briefly serving as a monk, was received by King Norodom Sihanouk and Queen Monineath at the palace after the ceremony. He later prayed at the Silver Pagoda, a palace temple with a solid silver floor.

In a statement from his cabinet, Ranariddh said: "I become a monk to learn the teachings of Buddhism and to clear my mind in order to have good character and show gratitude to my parents and compatriots."
Earlier in the week, Ranariddh said he hoped that entering the monkhood would also "calm his politics", an apparent reference to recent tensions with his coalition partner, co-Premier Hun Sen.
Ranariddh will enter Than Temple in Phnom Penh and travel to India for a one-day trip on Monday as part of his monkhood, his cabinet said.
